phase_name: Interactive Workflow End-to-End Independent Verification & Operational Readiness Certification
summary: Independently, adversarially re-verified the complete Interactive Workflow subsystem delivered across Phases 143K-143O against IWC-001 v1.1, CHGR-001 v1.0, TAMC-001, and TAMPC-001, trusting no prior implementation report, docstring, or comment. Read all four contracts and every phase report 143J/143I.1/143I.2/143K/143L/143M/143N/143O in full, plus every .py file (46 files) under src/pcae/interactive_workflow/. Independently re-derived the ownership model for all ten IWC-001 v1.1 session responsibilities (transition legality, transition sequencing, evidence registration, clarification lifecycle, audit recording, preview construction, Preview Digest generation, confirmation lifecycle, orchestration sequencing, publication readiness) directly against source and confirmed each has exactly one production owner, with one disclosed exception: validation/invariants.py's validate_terminal_integrity independently re-implements a transition-legality check (calling is_valid_transition directly) that state_machine/validator.py's TransitionValidator also performs, contradicting that module's 'sole owner' docstring claim -- both consult the same canonical TRANSITION_TABLE with no divergence found, classified Non-Blocking (N-1). Independently reconstructed the intra-package dependency graph (confirmed acyclic; the one documented near-cycle risk in state_machine/engine.py is correctly broken via a deferred function-scope import) and confirmed zero cross-module private-attribute access. Independently confirmed authority neutrality: grep for 'interactive_workflow' in src/pcae/cli.py and elsewhere in src/pcae returns zero matches (the package is wired into nothing outside itself), and a full-package keyword sweep for publish/notify/create_chgr/invoke_lifecycle/subprocess/requests/urllib/os.system/smtplib returns only prose/docstring hits, no callable capability. Independently cross-checked IWC-001 v1.1 section 4.4's ten-state transition table against state_machine/transitions.py's TRANSITION_TABLE: exact match, no extras, no omissions. Independently constructed and ran eleven adversarial attacks directly against the live running code (not simulated): illegal transition skipping stages, terminal-state replay, self-transition, duplicate evidence registration, forged/stale preview digest confirmation, replayed confirmation response, confirmation against a stale transition-sequence number, malformed digest verification, publication-package construction from a non-Confirmed session, direct invocation of SessionCoordinator.perform_publication(), and malformed session/evidence/confirmation identifiers -- every attack failed deterministically with a distinct, specific, typed error, with no partial mutation. Ran pcae check/health/doctor(execution-chain,task-memory,git-lock,hooks)/push check/runtime inspect directly; runtime confirmed Observed/observe/unavailable, unchanged before and after. See docs/PHASE_143P_INTERACTIVE_WORKFLOW_END_TO_END_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_AND_OPERATIONAL_READINESS_CERTIFICATION.md.

verdict: CERTIFIED -- the Interactive Workflow subsystem implemented across Phases 143K-143O is operationally ready within its implemented scope, independently and adversarially re-verified from primary evidence (contract text and running code), not adopted from any prior phase's own narrative. This certification is explicitly not an authorization to execute governance workflows: the subsystem remains structurally incapable of publishing an artifact, creating a Canonical Human Governance Record, invoking PCAE lifecycle authority, or changing the runtime's capability. One Non-Blocking finding (N-1: a disclosed, non-divergent duplicated transition-legality check) and one Observation (O-1: an intentionally-unused TransitionEngine collaborator on WorkflowOrchestrator, disclosed in the code's own comment) were found; neither defeats certification and no repair was required. No implementation change was made by this phase.
